items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: when I joined the band... Duke got up on the piano... he said 'come here' to me 'sit down by the piano.' He explained to me how he voiced 'Caravan.'

ctx.x: I said “oh really?” And so I exchanged those for a blue sweater. But they both had that great originality that you look for, that you strive for, and it came natural for them. You know Ellington never really went to school to learn how to write music. And Strayhorn may have had a little bit, but they had that God-given talent to be able to sit down and write music but it was strictly their style. They weren’t getting it from somebody else. It was, there it was. In the voicing in the reed section, the voicings in…
the great Duke Ellington is taking time out to show me some voicings. Other band leaders have been striving, trying to figure out what did he do there, how did he voice that.
